purpose: Independent, source-reviewed partial relevance labels for four diagnostic retrieval queries. Not a comprehensive gold set or downstream agent efficacy test. Created without running retrieval or inspecting ranks. Held out from candidate optimization until code freeze.

metric_contract.positive_queries: Report relevant Hit@5 and reciprocal rank of first listed relevant ID; other returned IDs are unjudged, not necessarily irrelevant. Do not calculate complete Recall or false-positive precision from these partial labels.
metric_contract.delivery: For each retrieved labelled relevant item, verify its context carries the matching revision and all specified mandatory resource suffixes; missing retrieval and budget omission must be distinct.
metric_contract.judgment_limits: Single assessor/source-grounded labels, four queries, candidate-only corpus, no human validation or production representativeness claim. No forbidden-ID labels are imposed: broader companion skills may also be useful.

cases.relevance: TorchNPU nonblocking transfer finished submitting but pinned RAM remains occupied; when may a CPU buffer be reused?
cases.rationale: The pinned-host allocator procedure distinguishes CPU ownership, pending copy events, active/cached RAM, and completion before reuse; device-HBM tuning is a separate domain.

cases.relevance: Checkpoint loading got faster on the second run. Does high disk utilization prove the SSD is the bottleneck, or could cached reads explain it?
cases.rationale: The procedure requires a warm/cold/unknown cache ledger and corroborating queue/latency/workload evidence; utilization alone does not establish storage saturation.

cases.relevance: After asynchronous training save staging completes, may the next checkpoint overwrite its cached CPU snapshot while the previous writer is still uploading?
cases.rationale: The DCP completion table separates source-mutation readiness after staging from cached-snapshot reuse only after previous upload completion.

cases.relevance: SGLang video generation request timed out and its job record was deleted. How can I tell whether the worker stopped computing and released its resident components?
cases.rationale: The SGLang diffusion procedure distinguishes socket timeout/store deletion from worker/device completion and component-use residency; its source shows abort remains TODO.
